narrative.overview: A calm white page with one deep-blue ink, where the evidence is the real work: product screenshots and prototype clips, sourced figures, plain headings. It reads like the notebook of a designer who used to be an engineer, precise and quiet, with nothing on the page that is not doing a job.
keyCharacteristics: White ground with a soft blue wash across the top of the viewport, never a flat tint.
One accent, ledger blue, for links, the heading dot, selected tabs and figures.
White cards held off the white ground by soft shadow, not borders.
Screenshots framed on panels tinted with the prototype's own colour.
Text spans its column end to end; no reading-measure caps.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Ledger blue is the only accent the page itself owns. Any other colour on screen belongs to a product being shown.

rules.name: The Wash-Is-A-Gradient Rule
rules.body: The blue wash is always two soft radial blooms on a fixed layer; a flat tinted ground is never used.

rules.name: The Two Faces Rule
rules.body: League Spartan and Mulish carry everything; Plex Mono is a label face, never a voice.

rules.name: The End-To-End Rule
rules.body: No heading or paragraph gets a max-width or text-balance.

rules.name: The No-Border Card Rule
rules.body: Cards never carry a border; the soft shadow alone holds them off the ground.

dos: Do frame real product screenshots on a panel tinted with that product's own colour.
Do keep one figure per card, sourced, set in the prototype's colour.
Do tag every link, button and card with its analytics event (CLAUDE.md).
Do keep 44px touch targets and the single 2px ledger-blue focus ring.
donts: Don't add borders to cards or a coloured left border to anything.
Don't use a flat tinted page ground; the wash is a gradient.
Don't cap text width or balance headings.
Don't put a facts table of icon-and-label columns on the homepage (removed 11 Nov 2026).
Don't use em-dashes in copy, eyebrows above headings, or emoji as icons.
